Testing a generator package

Source: vignettes/generator-packages.Rmd
generator-packages.Rmd
library(zurngtest)

A package that provides random number generators should be able to say how its streams do in ‘PractRand’, the test suite the literature on generator design reports against. This article shows two ways to do that with zurngtest: from R, with any function that returns the generator’s bits, and from C, where ‘PractRand’ reads the generator’s words with no R in the loop.

The examples use zurand, a package of counter-based generators.

From R

pract_fun() turns any R function that returns n words into a source. zurand’s generators are stateless: rng_bits(key, n) is the first n words of the stream that key names. A long stream therefore takes each chunk from its own substream, rng_fold(key, i) for the ith chunk, the way zurand describes substreams.

library(zurand)

key <- rng_key(2024)
chunk <- 0
philox_words <- function(n) {
  chunk <<- chunk + 1
  words <- rng_bits(rng_fold(key, chunk), n, bits = 32)
  # 32-bit values as doubles, to the integers with the same bit patterns
  words[words >= 2^31] <- words[words >= 2^31] - 2^32
  suppressWarnings(as.integer(words))
}

pract_test(pract_fun(philox_words), min_bytes = 2^20, max_bytes = 2^22)
#> PractRand 0.96 test of function philox_words, 32-bit words
#> length= 1 megabyte (2^20 bytes)
#>   no anomalies in 80 test result(s)
#> length= 2 megabytes (2^21 bytes)
#>   no anomalies in 90 test result(s)
#> length= 4 megabytes (2^22 bytes)
#>   no anomalies in 99 test result(s)
#> No failure, time= 0.5 seconds

Runs this short are smoke tests. ‘PractRand’ results that matter for a generator come from runs of gigabytes to terabytes, which belong in a continuous-integration job or a long-running session rather than in a package’s checks on CRAN.

From C

A generator written in C runs fastest when ‘PractRand’ asks it for words directly. zurngtest registers a C function for that, declared in its header zurngtest.h. A generator package adds zurngtest to LinkingTo (and to Suggests), writes a fill function, and calls zurngtest_test_cfun() from C code that R calls through .Call():

#include <zurngtest.h>

typedef struct { uint32_t x; } xorshift32;

static void fill(void *state, uint32_t *out, size_t n) {
  xorshift32 *g = state;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    g->x ^= g->x << 13;
    g->x ^= g->x >> 17;
    g->x ^= g->x << 5;
    out[i] = g->x;
  }
}

SEXP test_xorshift32(SEXP options) {
  xorshift32 g = {2463534242u};
  return zurngtest_test_cfun(fill, &g, options);
}

options is a named list of pract_test()‘s other arguments, such as list(min_bytes = 2^20, max_bytes = 2^30), and the result is the same data frame pract_test() returns. The function is found with R_GetCCallable(), so nothing links to zurngtest at build time, and the fill function runs on the main thread. Through this path zurngtest tests words at about the speed of ’PractRand’’s own RNG_test.

zurand’s own tests build a small package against both headers and test a zurand stream this way.

Reading a result

The result has one row per test and length, with ‘PractRand’’s own evaluation. Its failed_at attribute is the first length at which any result was a failure, or NA:

lcg_low_bits <- local({
  x <- 1
  function(n) {
    out <- raw(n)
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      x <<- (1664525 * x + 1013904223) %% 2^32
      out[i] <- as.raw(x %% 256)
    }
    out
  }
})
res <- pract_test(pract_fun(lcg_low_bits, bits = 8), min_bytes = 2^12, max_bytes = 2^16)
attr(res, "failed_at")
#> [1] 4096
head(as.data.frame(res)[order(res$p_value), ], 3)
#>   bytes       test p_value    evaluation
#> 3  4096   Gap-16:A       0 FAIL !!!!!!!!
#> 4  4096   Gap-16:B       0 FAIL !!!!!!!!
#> 8  4096 FPF/16:all       0  FAIL !!!!!!!

The low byte of a power-of-two linear congruential generator repeats every 256 values, which ‘PractRand’ finds in the first few kilobytes.
